Prealgebra · Lesson 2.5

Powers of Powers

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Back in section 2.2 you found that raising a power to a power multiplies the two exponents. That one rule stretches much further than it first looks. It still works when three or more exponents are stacked, when the inside is a fraction, when an exponent turns negative or zero, and even when a number sits out in front of the variable. This last section puts every law in the chapter to work at once.

Problem
A glassblower mixes a colour by the ratio 7227​, and a deeper batch needs that ratio cubed, (72)3(27​)3. Find it two ways. First multiply the fraction by itself three times. Then cube the top and the bottom on their own, 73232373​. Give the value as a fraction.
Show a hint
  • Multiplying 72×72×7227​×27​×27​ collects every top together and every bottom together.
  • The tops give 73=34373=343 and the bottoms give 23=823=8. Both methods build the same fraction.
Show the full solution
Multiplying the fraction by itself three times gives three 7s on top and three 2s on the bottom. (72)3=7×7×72×2×2=7323=3438(27​)3=2×2×27×7×7​=2373​=8343​ The value is 34388343​​. Cubing the top and the bottom on their own is the same work written more directly.
Problem
Test the same idea on a fourth power so it is not just a quirk of cubing. A kite design scales the ratio 3553​ to the fourth power. Send the exponent onto the top and the bottom separately, 34545434​, and give the value as a fraction.
Show a hint
  • The exponent lands on both the top and the bottom, so work out 3434 and 5454 each.
  • One of them is 34=8134=81. Work out 5454 yourself and stack it underneath.
Show the full solution
Send the exponent onto the top and the bottom separately. (35)4=3454=81625(53​)4=5434​=62581​ The value is 8162562581​​. Four copies of 3553​ gather four 3s on top and four 5s on the bottom, so the rule is not special to cubing.
Key idea
Power of a quotient. An outer exponent applies to the top and the bottom alike. (ab)n=anbn(b≠0)(ba​)n=bnan​(b=0) A fraction raised to the nn means nn copies of the whole fraction multiplied together, so nn tops multiply over nn bottoms. It is the power-of-a-product rule for a fraction.

Two stacked exponents multiply. Three stacked exponents do the same thing, since the rule just fires twice. Peel the outermost exponent off first, then handle what is left.

Problem
A folding screen carries a motif repeated 2222 times across one panel. A room divider holds (22)3(22)3 such panels in a grid, and an exhibition lines up ((22)3)2((22)3)2 of those dividers. Simplify the whole tower ((22)3)2((22)3)2 to a single power of 2 and give the exponent.
Show a hint
  • Peel off the outermost exponent first. The power rule turns ((22)3)2((22)3)2 into (22)3×2(22)3×2.
  • Now (22)6=22×6(22)6=22×6. All three exponents end up multiplied together.
Show the full solution
Work from the outside in, using the power rule each time. ((22)3)2=(22)3×2=(22)6=22×6=212((22)3)2=(22)3×2=(22)6=22×6=212 The exponent is 1212​. Every exponent in the tower ends up multiplied together, 2×3×2=122×3×2=12.
Problem
An elevator panel shows the reading (94)0(94)0. Without a calculator, give its exact value.
Show a hint
  • Multiply the stacked exponents first, 4×04×0, or recall what any nonzero base to the zero power is.
  • Whichever route you take, the panel settles on the value that every nonzero base shares at the zero power.
Show the full solution
Multiply the exponents, (94)0=94×0=90=1(94)0=94×0=90=1, so the panel reads 11​. You can also skip the multiplying, since any nonzero base to the zero power is already 1.

Watch your step here, because this is the single most common slip in the whole chapter. Stacking exponents multiplies them, while multiplying powers of the same base adds them. They look alike on the page and do opposite things to the exponents.

Problem
A cargo line runs two belts. The upper belt batches packages as (53)2(53)2, and the lower belt batches them as 53×5253×52. They are not the same count. Rewrite each as a single power of 5, then give the difference of the two exponents, the upper belt exponent minus the lower belt exponent.
Show a hint
  • The upper belt is a power raised to a power, so multiply its exponents. The lower belt is a product of powers, so add its exponents.
  • Upper is 53×2=5653×2=56 and lower is 53+2=5553+2=55. Subtract the two exponents.
Show the full solution
The upper belt stacks a power on a power, so the exponents multiply, (53)2=53×2=56(53)2=53×2=56. The lower belt multiplies two powers of the same base, so the exponents add, 53×52=53+2=5553×52=53+2=55. The difference is 6−5=16−5=1​. These are the two rules people mix up most, and they do opposite things to the exponents.

The power rule does not require the inner exponent to be positive. Try a negative inner exponent and check that multiplying the exponents still gives the right answer.

Problem
A sound desk stores the faint gain 2−32−3, then a sharpening step squares whatever is stored, computing (2−3)2(2−3)2. Multiply the exponents just as always and write the result as a single power of 2 with one exponent. Give that exponent.
Show a hint
  • The power rule multiplies the exponents even when one of them is negative.
  • Carry the sign through the multiplication, so the inner −3−3 meets the outer 22. The product is the new exponent.
Show the full solution
Multiply the exponents, sign and all. (2−3)2=2(−3)×2=2−6(2−3)2=2(−3)×2=2−6 The exponent is −6−6​. Written without a negative that is 126=164261​=641​, so squaring a small number made it smaller still.
Key idea
Stacked exponents multiply. Raising a power to a power multiplies the exponents, and for a stack of exponents you multiply every one of them. ((am)n)p=am×n×p((am)n)p=am×n×p Each outer layer is the power rule applied again. Signs make no difference. A negative inner exponent stays negative under a positive outer one, and a zero anywhere makes the whole thing a0=1a0=1.

Now put a number in front of the variable. When an outer exponent sits on something like 2x32x3, it is tempting to leave the 22 alone. You cannot. Everything inside the parentheses is a product, and the coefficient is one of its factors, so the exponent lands on it too.

Problem
A bakery stamps trays of cookies, each tray holding 2x32x3 rows where xx is the dough setting. A holiday order raises that whole tray to the fourth power, (2x3)4(2x3)4. One apprentice writes 2x122x12 and another writes 16x1216x12. Exactly one is right. Give the correct simplified form. Type it in the form such as 16x^12.
Show a hint
  • The outer 4 grips every factor inside the parentheses, both the 22 and the x3x3. Do not leave the 22 untouched.
  • One factor gives 24=1624=16. Send the same 44 onto x3x3 yourself and combine the two pieces.
Show the full solution
The outer exponent lands on every factor inside, the coefficient included. (2x3)4=24×(x3)4=16×x12=16x12(2x3)4=24×(x3)4=16×x12=16x12 The correct form is 16x1216x12​. The apprentice who wrote 2x122x12 forgot to raise the 22.
Key idea
The outer exponent applies to the coefficient. An outer exponent applies to the number in front as well as to the variable. (c xm)n=cn xm×n(cxm)n=cnxm×n The coefficient is another factor inside the parentheses, so the exponent applies to it as it does to xx. A common mistake is to write (2x3)4(2x3)4 as 2x122x12 instead of 16x1216x12.

One more case ties the negative powers from the last section to the quotient rule from this one. Make the outer exponent negative while it sits on a fraction, and the fraction flips over.

Problem
A recipe scales to 2332​ strength, but a reset raises that whole setting to the power −3−3. Evaluate (23)−3(32​)−3. Treat the negative exponent as a reciprocal first, flipping 2332​ over, then cube. Give the value as a fraction.
Show a hint
  • A negative exponent takes the reciprocal of the base, and the reciprocal of 2332​ is 3223​.
  • So (23)−3=(32)3=3323(32​)−3=(23​)3=2333​.
Show the full solution
The negative exponent flips the fraction and turns positive. (23)−3=(32)3=3323=278(32​)−3=(23​)3=2333​=827​ The answer is 278827​​. Flip first, then send the exponent onto the new top and the new bottom.
Key idea
A negative outer exponent gives the reciprocal. A fraction raised to a negative power equals its reciprocal raised to the positive power. (ab)−n=(ba)n=bnan(a,b≠0)(ba​)−n=(ab​)n=anbn​(a,b=0) Take the reciprocal, then apply the exponent to the new top and bottom.
Fun fact
Stacked exponents grow at a pace the mind cannot picture. The tidy looking tower ((103)3)3((103)3)3 multiplies out to 10271027, a number with twenty seven zeros, already more than the estimated count of every grain of sand on every beach on Earth. And that is the gentle kind of tower. A true tower where each exponent is itself a full power, like 22222222, reaches 65536 in just four 2s, and one floor higher the number is too long to write on this page. Mathematicians invented a whole separate notation, called up-arrows, just to tame them.

These laws can all show up in a single expression. A power of a quotient, a raised coefficient, and the quotient rule can sit in the same problem, with order of operations deciding what comes first. Work one grouped piece at a time.

Problem
A lighting rig simplifies (3x4)2x5x5(3x4)2​ to a single coefficient and power of xx. Find it. Type it in the form such as 16x^12.
Show a hint
  • Raise the numerator first. The outer 2 lands on the 33 and on the x4x4.
  • The top becomes 9x89x8. Now divide by x5x5 with the quotient rule, subtracting the exponents, and keep the 99.
Show the full solution
Open the numerator, letting the outer exponent hit both factors. (3x4)2=32×x4×2=9x8(3x4)2=32×x4×2=9x8 Now divide by x5x5. The coefficient is untouched by the division, and the quotient rule subtracts the variable exponents. 9x8x5=9x8−5=9x3x59x8​=9x8−5=9x3 The answer is 9x39x3​.
Problem
A power grid balances two terms. Simplify (x32)2×(x22)−3(2x3​)2×(2x2​)−3 to a single number with no variable left. Find that number.
Show a hint
  • The first term lands on the top and the bottom, (x3)222=x6422(x3)2​=4x6​. The second has a negative outer exponent, so flip it first.
  • Flipping gives (2x2)3=8x6(x22​)3=x68​. Now multiply the two fractions and watch the xx cancel.
Show the full solution
The first term sends the exponent onto the top and the bottom. (x32)2=(x3)222=x64(2x3​)2=22(x3)2​=4x6​ The second has a negative outer exponent, so flip the fraction first, then raise it, coefficient and all. (x22)−3=(2x2)3=23(x2)3=8x6(2x2​)−3=(x22​)3=(x2)323​=x68​ Multiply the two results. x64×8x6=8x64x6=2x6−6=24x6​×x68​=4x68x6​=2x6−6=2 The answer is 22​.

Here is the capstone, one expression that uses every law in the chapter. There is a coefficient inside a flip, a quotient under an exponent, a tower of three powers, and the quotient rule. Work one grouped piece at a time.

Problem
Evaluate ((2x3)24x4)3×(x22)−3.(4x4(2x3)2​)3×(2x2​)−3. It is built so the variable cancels completely and a single number remains. Find that number.
Show a hint
  • Simplify deep inside the first parentheses before applying the outer 3. Raise (2x3)2=4x6(2x3)2=4x6, then divide by 4x44x4 to get a clean x2x2 with coefficient 11.
  • The first factor becomes (x2)3=x6(x2)3=x6. The second has a negative outer exponent, so flip x222x2​ to 2x2x22​ before cubing. Then multiply and watch the xx disappear.
Show the full solution
Work the first factor from the inside out. The inner top is (2x3)2=22x6=4x6(2x3)2=22x6=4x6, and dividing by 4x44x4 gives 4x64x4=44 x6−4=x2.4x44x6​=44​x6−4=x2. The outer exponent then multiplies, (x2)3=x6(x2)3=x6. The second factor has a negative outer exponent, so flip the fraction, then raise top and bottom. (x22)−3=(2x2)3=23(x2)3=8x6(2x2​)−3=(x22​)3=(x2)323​=x68​ Multiply the two pieces. x6×8x6=8 x6−6=8x0=8x6×x68​=8x6−6=8x0=8 The number is 88​.

Practice these ideas

Practice
You already know that stacking a power on a power multiplies the two exponents. This section pushes that idea everywhere it can go, onto fractions, onto coefficients, up nested towers, and across negative exponents, until every law in the chapter can show up in one expression at once.
Practice
A canyon guide tests an echo by stacking it on itself. One shout returns as (42)3(42)3 faint repeats. Rewrite that as a single power of 44 and give the exponent.
Show the solution
Stacking a power on a power multiplies the two exponents rather than adding them. (42)3=42×3=46(42)3=42×3=46 The exponent is 66​. The outer 33 asks for three copies of 4242, and each copy carries two factors of 44, so there are 2×3=62×3=6 factors in all.
Practice
A quilter sews a block by raising a small square to a power. The block holds (23)4(32​)4 of one unit of fabric. Write that as a single fraction.
Show the solution
An outer exponent on a quotient lands on both the top and the bottom. (23)4=2434=1681(32​)4=3424​=8116​ The block is 16818116​​ of a unit. Four copies of 2332​ multiplied together gather four 22s on top and four 33s on the bottom.
Practice
An outer exponent on a fraction lands on the top and the bottom alike, so (ab)n=anbn(ba​)n=bnan​ for any nonzero bb. It works because multiplying nn copies of abba​ gathers nn factors of aa on top and nn factors of bb on the bottom.
Practice
On a beadwork loom a single tile pattern is enlarged by raising it to the fourth power. The tile is described by 2b32b3, so the enlarged pattern is (2b3)4(2b3)4. Simplify it to a coefficient times a single power of bb.
Show the solution
The outer exponent reaches every factor inside, coefficient included. (2b3)4=24×(b3)4=16×b3×4=16b12(2b3)4=24×(b3)4=16×b3×4=16b12 The pattern simplifies to 16b1216b12​. It is not 2b122b12, and forgetting to raise the 22 is the most common slip here.
Practice
When a product inside parentheses carries a number out front, the outer exponent lands on that number too, so (k xm)n=kn xmn(kxm)n=knxmn. For example (2x3)4=16x12(2x3)4=16x12, never 2x122x12. The coefficient is a factor like any other, so it cannot be left behind.
Practice
Two coral reef readings look alike but mean different things. The first colony grows as (52)3(52)3 polyps, a power stacked on a power. The second grows as 52×5352×53 polyps, two powers multiplied together. Both fold to a single power of 55. By how much does the first reading's exponent beat the second reading's exponent?
Show the solution
Stacking a power on a power multiplies the exponents, while multiplying two powers of the same base adds them. (52)3=52×3=56,52×53=52+3=55(52)3=52×3=56,52×53=52+3=55 The first reading reaches exponent 66 and the second reaches 55, so stacking pulls ahead by 6−5=16−5=1​.
Practice
A lantern festival dims a light by raising a faint setting to a power. The setting is 2−32−3 of full brightness, and squaring it gives (2−3)2(2−3)2. Write the result as a single power of 22 and give the exponent.
Show the solution
Multiply the two exponents, sign and all. (2−3)2=2(−3)×2=2−6(2−3)2=2(−3)×2=2−6 The exponent is −6−6​. Two copies of 2−32−3 put six factors of 22 in the denominator, which is 164641​.
Practice
Stacking really does outrun adding. Starting from 104104, multiplying by another 103103 only reaches 107107, but raising it to the 33rd power leaps to 10121012. That gap of five zeros is the difference between joining copies and making copies of copies.
Practice
A model railway sets its scale as a fraction, then a reversing switch raises that scale to the power −2−2. The scale is 3553​, so the switch produces (35)−2(53​)−2. Write the result as a single fraction.
Show the solution
A negative outer exponent flips the fraction, then the exponent goes positive. (35)−2=(53)2=5232=259(53​)−2=(35​)2=3252​=925​ The switch produces 259925​​. The flip handles the minus sign, and the squaring lands on the new top and the new bottom.
Practice
A negative outer exponent on a fraction turns it upside down and makes the exponent positive, so (ab)−n=(ba)n(ba​)−n=(ab​)n for nonzero aa and bb. The minus sign is really just the reciprocal rule applied to a fraction.
Practice
A fractal antenna is etched in stages. Each stage splits every arm into 2222 smaller arms, and the design runs through three stages, so the tip count builds up as the nested tower ((22)2)2((22)2)2. When three exponents are stacked, all of them multiply together. Rewrite the tower as a single power of 22 and give its exponent.
Show the solution
Every stacked exponent multiplies into the next. ((22)2)2=2 2×2×2=28((22)2)2=22×2×2=28 The exponent is 88​, so the tip count is 256256.
Practice
A salt cavern records its volume as (2c2)3(2c2)3 and the brine it holds as 4c54c5. The packing density is the volume divided by the brine, (2c2)34c54c5(2c2)3​. Simplify it to a coefficient times a single power of cc.
Show the solution
Open the top with the power of a product rule, raising the coefficient too. (2c2)3=23×c2×3=8c6(2c2)3=23×c2×3=8c6 Now divide, splitting the coefficients from the powers of cc. 8c64c5=84×c6−5=2c1=2c4c58c6​=48​×c6−5=2c1=2c The packing density simplifies to 2c2c​.
Practice
A tuning fork's overtone strength is modeled by (a2)3×(a−3)2(a2)3×(a−3)2 for a nonzero aa. Simplify each tower first, then combine. The messy expression collapses to something tiny. What is its value?
Show the solution
Multiply within each tower, then add when the powers meet. (a2)3=a6,(a−3)2=a−6(a2)3=a6,(a−3)2=a−6 a6×a−6=a6+(−6)=a0=1a6×a−6=a6+(−6)=a0=1 Any nonzero base to the zero power is 11, so the whole thing folds to 11​.
Practice
A tower of exponents grows almost too fast to picture. Stacking just (((22)2)2)2(((22)2)2)2 multiplies four twos to 216216, already past sixty thousand. A few more floors and the number would dwarf the count of grains of sand on Earth.
Practice
A wind chime nests three tunings. The deepest tube rings as ((22)3)2((22)3)2 and a damper divides that ring by (24)2(24)2. The audible tone is ((22)3)2(24)2(24)2((22)3)2​. Write it as a single power of 22 and give its value.
Show the solution
Collapse each tower by multiplying all of its stacked exponents. On top, three exponents multiply. ((22)3)2=22×3×2=212((22)3)2=22×3×2=212 On the bottom, two multiply. (24)2=24×2=28(24)2=24×2=28 Now divide a common base by subtracting. 21228=212−8=24=1628212​=212−8=24=16 The audible tone is 1616​.
Practice
A foundry mixes powers of 22 and 55 into one casting reading, (23×5102)−2.(10223×5​)−2. Simplify the whole thing to a single fraction.
Show the solution
Settle the inside first. The top is 23×5=8×5=4023×5=8×5=40 and the bottom is 102=100102=100. 23×5102=40100=2510223×5​=10040​=52​ Now the negative outer exponent flips the fraction, then squares it on both top and bottom. (25)−2=(52)2=254(52​)−2=(25​)2=425​ The casting reading is 254425​​.
Practice
A beehive arranges its active brood cells by a single formula, (23)4×(2−2)3(24)2.(24)2(23)4×(2−2)3​. Every law in this chapter shows up once. Collapse it all into a single power of 22 and give that power's exponent.
Show the solution
Flatten every stacked power first, multiplying the exponents and carrying the signs. (23)4=212,(2−2)3=2−6,(24)2=28(23)4=212,(2−2)3=2−6,(24)2=28 Multiply the two powers on top by adding their exponents. 212×2−6=212+(−6)=26212×2−6=212+(−6)=26 Then divide by subtracting the bottom exponent. 2628=26−8=2−22826​=26−8=2−2 The exponent is −2−2​, and the whole formula is 1441​.
